decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Preparing to select three Pokémon for the Showdown battle.

Reviewing the roster to pick a balanced three-Pokémon team.

Evaluating matchup risks and coverage for the three chosen Pokémon.

Garchomp's Focus Sash guarantees Stealth Rock entry. Corviknight's Mirror Armor reflects stat drops. The six roster options are being weighed for a balanced core.

Three potential cores are being weighed: Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Dragonite; Primarina, Garchomp, and Kingambit; or Gholdengo, Dragonite, and Corviknight. The matchup between Gholdengo and Kingambit is being analyzed to determine which special moves land effectively.

Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is not very effective against Kingambit because Dark resists Ghost. Kingambit's Iron Head is also weak against Gholdengo. The analysis continues with Kowtow Cleave.

Kowtow Cleave is super effective against Gholdengo. Sucker Punch also lands hard. Kingambit beats Gholdengo. Dragonite's Earthquake hits Gholdengo super effectively. Dragonite's Ice Punch is weak.

Dragonite's Earthquake is super effective against Gholdengo. Primarina's Moonblast is also super effective against Dragonite.

Hyper Voice is Water-type with Liquid Voice, so it is resisted by Dragonite. Garchomp's Earthquake is neutral against Primarina.

Primarina's Ice Beam is four times super effective against Garchomp. Garchomp's Poison Jab threatens Primarina. Kingambit's Iron Head is neutral against Primarina.

Corviknight's Body Press hits Kingambit four times super effectively. Kingambit's Dark moves are resisted by Primarina's Fairy typing, so it cannot threaten her offensively. Primarina can safely set up with Calm Mind.

Body Press misses Gholdengo. The scripted opponent will likely bring a defensive or control team. A strong offensive core is being chosen: Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Primarina for coverage and setup; or Dragonite, Gholdengo, and Kingambit for priority and Multiscale.

Gholdengo and Kingambit do not cover each other well against certain threats, though their combined roster handles many opponents. The scripted opponent may bring a bulky control team or similar strong attackers. Dragonite's DD sweep is being weighed as the primary win condition, supported by Multiscale, Yache Berry, Extreme Speed, and coverage moves. Kingambit's SD + Supreme Overlord is also being considered for late-game strength.

Gholdengo's Nasty Plot is being weighed with Good as Gold and Life Orb. Corviknight is a support pivot, Garchomp is fragile, and Primarina is slower but strong. Dragonite, Gholdengo, and Kingambit form the chosen offensive core. A matchup matrix is being built for this trio against possible opponent mons. Dragonite's Ice Punch is four times super effective against Garchomp. Earthquake is also super effective against Garchomp.

Dragonite's Earthquake is neutral against Garchomp. Ice Punch is four times super effective against it. Against Corviknight, Dragonite's Earthquake is super effective but its Ice Punch is resisted. Against Gholdengo and Kingambit, Earthquake is super effective while Ice Punch is resisted.

Dragonite's speed is likely tied with the opponent's if both use identical spreads. Against Primarina, Dragonite's Earthquake and Ice Punch are neutral while Primarina's Moonblast and Ice Beam are super effective; the Yache Berry halves ice damage once. Gholdengo's Make It Rain is neutral against Garchomp.

Garchomp outspeeds Gholdengo and can OHKO it with Earthquake. Gholdengo wins against Corviknight because Body Press misses Ghost. Against Kingambit, Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark typing.

Gholdengo outspeeds Dragonite and can land Shadow Ball or Nasty Plot. Multiscale halves the first hit. Gholdengo's Make It Rain is resisted by Kingambit's Dark typing. Kingambit is bulky so it might survive a two-hit KO. Against Primarina both moves are neutral.

Gholdengo's Steel typing resists Primarina's Fairy and Water moves, so it can safely KO her. Kingambit's Iron Head, Kowtow Cleave, and Sucker Punch are all neutral against Garchomp, though Garchomp outspeeds it with Earthquake.

Corviknight's Body Press is four times super effective against Kingambit. Mirror Armor reflects stat drops, so a Stealth Rock setup would not be reflected back. Against Gholdengo, Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch are both super effective, but Iron Head is resisted; if Gholdengo uses Nasty Plot, Sucker Punch fails. Kingambit and Gholdengo tie in speed at 70.

The Dragonite, Gholdengo, and Kingambit core is being abandoned. Primarina beats both Dragonite and Kingambit, leaving Gholdengo as the only viable check. Kingambit also struggles against Corviknight's Body Press and Garchomp's Earthquake. The trio lacks reliable coverage.

A new core is being considered: Gholdengo, Primarina, and Kingambit. Primarina would handle Dragonite and Garchomp with Ice Beam and Moonblast. Gholdengo would cover Corviknight and status effects. Kingambit would threaten Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave. The concern remains that Corviknight's Body Press would destroy Kingambit if it leads.

Primarina cannot break Corviknight. All of her moves are resisted by Steel, and Body Press is neutral against both types. Gholdengo beats Corviknight instead. Make It Rain and Shadow Ball are neutral, and Body Press misses Ghost.

Dragonite's Earthquake is super effective against Corviknight. The core is being reconsidered as the best balanced option again, since Dragonite's Ice Punch and Earthquake cover opposing dragons and steels.

A new core is being considered: Dragonite, Gholdengo, and Primarina. This removes Kingambit from the lineup. Gholdengo would be harder for the opponent to bring down, since Primarina cannot threaten it well. Dragonite would still land Earthquake on Gholdengo.

Dragonite outspeeds Kingambit by 62 points. Earthquake is super effective against it. A rough calculation suggests Dragonite could OHKO Kingambit with no bulk investment.

Garchomp is being weighed as a lead option. Stealth Rock would chip away at Multiscale and break Focus Sash, though fewer switches in a 3v3 reduce hazard value. A Focus Sash Garchomp could reliably land rocks and trade. It would threaten Fairy types with Poison Jab, Steels with Earthquake, and Dragons with Dragon Claw.

The scripted opponent is a control bot that likely switches often, so Stealth Rock becomes more valuable. Mega Evolution appears unavailable since no mega stones are present. The ideal three-pokemon lineup needs a lead to pressure immediately, a sweeper, and a revenge killer or answer to the opponent's sweeper.

The final lineup is Gholdengo, Dragonite, and Kingambit. Gholdengo leads because it outspeeds every other mon except Garchomp, and its Good as Gold blocks status moves. The opponent's team lacks any status-inflicting attacks, so that ability is less critical than expected.

If the opponent leads Primarina, Dragonite's Ice Beam is reduced to 1x damage by both Multiscale and Yache Berry. That makes it effectively neutral, so Dragonite can survive the hit and still land Earthquake.

Dragonite's Earthquake is ineffective against Flying-type opponents because Dragonite is Dragon/Flying. It would be completely immune to Ground moves. Dragon Claw would be the only viable physical attack in that matchup.

Dragonite is now the clear lead. It is immune to Ground moves, so Garchomp's Earthquake cannot land. Ice Punch OHKOs Garchomp. Earthquake destroys Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Corviknight. Its Yache Berry and Multiscale protect it from Primarina's Ice Beam. Extreme Speed lets it revenge kill. Only Primarina's Moonblast poses a real threat.

Primarina's Moonblast is calculated at roughly 40 to 50 percent damage against Dragonite, breaking Multiscale. Dragonite leads the team, with Gholdengo and Kingambit in the back. Primarina is dropped from the lineup because she cannot reliably handle opposing Dragonite or Garchomp.

A speed tie with the opponent is too risky for a mirror match. Kingambit's Supreme Overlord makes it stronger when teammates faint, so keeping it in the back is ideal for late-game pressure. Replacing Kingambit with Primarina would remove the dedicated answer to opposing Gholdengo. Replacing Gholdengo with Primarina would sacrifice the special sweeper and status immunity.
